name: DDColor Photo Colorization
purpose: A batch photo colorization pipeline that bulk-ingests black-and-white scans to Backblaze B2, runs DDColor locally to produce full-color reconstructions at original resolution, and writes colorized outputs, side-by-side comparisons and a per-run manifest CSV back to B2 next to the untouched originals, so archives keep provenance and editorial teams can serve results through presigned URLs.
tagline: Colorize black-and-white photo archives with DDColor and keep every original and output in Backblaze B2.

features.title: Batches
features.summary: create, edit, delete and run colorization batches with a per-run manifest

features.title: Colorization
features.summary: DDColor runs locally (CUDA, Apple MPS or CPU) and keeps the original resolution

features.title: Photo Library
features.summary: grayscale originals with before/after views of every colorized version

features.title: Bulk Ingest
features.summary: drag-and-drop many scans straight to the grayscale prefix by presigned PUT

features.title: Dashboard
features.summary: photos ingested and colorized, derived bytes and the write-amplification ratio

features.title: Bucket Explorer
features.summary: browse, preview, download and delete any object in the bucket

features.title: Settings
features.summary: theme plus labelled demo preference fields

b2_surface.why: the browser bulk-ingests originals straight to the grayscale prefix
verify an ingested upload, read per-key size, and the /health connectivity probe
read an original for inference and read batch records
write colorized outputs, comparison images, manifest CSVs and batch records
the Photo Library, batch list, dashboard aggregates and the full-bucket explorer
serve originals, colorized images, comparisons and manifests to viewers and CMS import jobs
remove a batch's derived objects while keeping the originals, and Bucket Explorer deletes

stack.web: Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind v4, shadcn/ui, TanStack Query, Recharts
stack.api: FastAPI, Python 3.12+, boto3, Pydantic v2, Pillow, DDColor (PyTorch, optional ML extra)

env_vars.name: B2_APPLICATION_KEY_ID
env_vars.note: B2 application key ID (**keyID** in the B2 console)

env_vars.name: B2_APPLICATION_KEY
env_vars.note: B2 application key (**applicationKey**), shown once at creation

env_vars.name: B2_BUCKET_NAME
env_vars.note: bucket unique name (**Bucket Unique Name** in the B2 console)

env_vars.name: B2_REGION
env_vars.note: the region inside the bucket's **Endpoint** (`s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`); the S3 endpoint is derived from it

env_vars.name: B2_PUBLIC_URL_BASE
env_vars.note: public object base URL, when the bucket is public

env_vars.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL
env_vars.note: separate-origin deploys only; Next.js inlines it at build time

env_vars.name: DDCOLOR_DEVICE
env_vars.note: inference device: `auto` (default, CUDA then Apple MPS then CPU), `cpu`, `cuda` or `mps`

env_vars.name: HF_HOME
env_vars.note: cache directory for the DDColor weights downloaded from the Hugging Face Hub (no token needed)

env_vars.name: MODEL_DOWNLOAD_STALL_SECONDS
env_vars.note: seconds without new bytes before a first-use Hugging Face weight download fails its batch (default `120`)
